MSC Cruises — the European standard

MSC is the cruise line that most European first-time cruisers choose — and the choice is usually vindicated. Italian-founded, Swiss-owned, and European in character, MSC has invested aggressively in new ships over the past decade. The World-class ships (MSC World Europa, MSC Seashore, MSC Grandiosa) are among the most impressive in the industry.

What MSC does well

New fleet: the average age of MSC's active fleet is among the lowest in the industry. New ships mean larger cabins, more advanced technology, and better onboard infrastructure. The waterslides, pool decks, and common areas on the Meraviglia and World-class ships are genuinely impressive.

Children sail free: on the majority of MSC itineraries in the Mediterranean, children under 12 travel free when sharing a cabin with two full-paying adults. For a family of four, this is a saving of €800–1,200 on the cruise fare alone. Combined with the relatively low base fares, MSC makes family cruising affordable in a way that Norwegian and Royal Caribbean simply do not.

Cirque du Soleil: MSC's partnership produces at-sea shows that are categorically better than the standard cruise ship entertainment. The shows are included in the fare on ships that feature them.

The buffet: consistent quality, genuinely good Italian pizza and pasta, wide international selection. Breakfast is particularly strong.

Pricing: the most competitive in the European market for what you get. Interior cabin prices starting under €400/person for 7 nights in the Mediterranean make first-cruise decisions financially accessible.

Where MSC falls short

Service inconsistency: with ships carrying 4,000–5,000 passengers, service personalisation is limited. Staff are efficient and polite but not attentive in the way Celebrity or Norwegian are. Some cruisers find this adequate; others find it disappointing after reading about the experience they expected.

Overcrowding: large ships mean large crowds. Pool deck chair wars in summer, buffet queues at peak times, disembarkation queues that can stretch to 90 minutes. If you want space and calm, MSC's largest ships in peak season are not it.

Drinks package pricing: at €55–65/person/day, MSC's beverage packages are among the most expensive relative to the underlying quality. If you drink moderately, paying by the drink is more economical.

Who MSC is for: families with children under 12, first-time cruisers, budget-conscious travellers who want a new ship, and anyone who prefers a European atmosphere over an American one.

Search MSC cruises on CruiseDirect


Costa Cruises — the original Italian way

Costa has operated Mediterranean cruises longer than MSC, with an Italian character that is arguably more genuinely Italian — less polished, more lived-in, and with food that reflects the regional Italian cooking traditions more accurately than MSC's pan-international approach.

What Costa does well

Food quality at the main dining room: the pasta, risotto, and fish at Costa's included restaurant is consistently rated as the best among the three lines compared here. The kitchen takes the Italian cooking heritage seriously — fresh pasta properly cooked, regional dishes that change by itinerary, and desserts that are genuinely good rather than mass-produced. For travellers who care about what they eat at dinner, this matters.

Relaxed atmosphere: Costa ships feel less like managed entertainment environments and more like being on a large Italian holiday. There is less pressure to fill every hour with scheduled activities. You can sit on the deck and read without feeling like you are missing something. The pace is slower.

Value: Costa's lowest fares are the most competitive in the European market, occasionally undercutting MSC. Interior cabins from €369/person for 7 nights make Costa the genuine budget entry point into Mediterranean cruising.

Smaller ships (relative): Costa's fleet includes ships carrying 2,000–3,000 passengers alongside a few larger vessels. The smaller ships mean shorter queues, easier navigation, and a more proportionate human scale.

Where Costa falls short

Older fleet: Costa's average ship age is higher than MSC's. Older ships mean smaller cabins, less spectacular waterparks and deck facilities, and facilities that feel dated compared to the newest builds. The experience is perfectly adequate but not impressive in the way MSC's latest ships are.

Entertainment: Costa's evening shows and onboard entertainment programmes are less spectacular than MSC's Cirque partnership or Norwegian's Broadway shows. If evening entertainment is a priority, Costa underdelivers.

Announcement fatigue: like MSC, onboard announcements in multiple languages (Italian, English, Spanish, French, German) are a constant background presence. This bothers some passengers significantly and others not at all.

Who Costa is for: couples without children, travellers who prioritise food at dinner over activities, those who want the lowest possible entry price, and anyone who actively prefers a quieter, more relaxed atmosphere over choreographed entertainment.

Book Costa Cruises on CruiseDirect


Norwegian Cruise Line — total freedom

Norwegian invented "Freestyle Cruising" in 2000 and has refined the concept ever since. The premise is simple and genuinely different: no assigned dining time, no dress codes, no structured schedule. You design your onboard day rather than following one the cruise line designed for you.

What Norwegian does well

Freestyle Dining: the practical difference is significant. Traditional cruise lines have two dinner sittings — early (around 6 PM) and late (around 8:30 PM). You are assigned to one, sit with the same table companions each night, and eat at that time every evening. Norwegian has no sittings — you go to whatever restaurant you want, whenever you want, and are seated immediately or within a short wait. This flexibility, once experienced, makes fixed dining feel claustrophobic.

Dining variety: 15–20 venues per ship, from the included main dining room and buffet to specialty restaurants (Italian, steakhouse, Japanese, seafood, French) charged separately at €30–60/person. The quality at both the included and specialty venues exceeds MSC and Costa meaningfully — Norwegian's kitchen investment is genuine.

Ship design: Norwegian's Prima and Viva (launched 2022–2023) are exceptionally designed ships. The outdoor spaces, the pool areas, and the spa complex are industry-leading. The interior aesthetic is closer to a boutique hotel than a floating resort.

Entertainment: Broadway-calibre shows included in the fare, plus a range of on-deck entertainment and performances. Better than MSC/Costa, comparable to Royal Caribbean.

Where Norwegian falls short

Price: 30–50% more expensive than MSC/Costa for comparable itineraries. On a 7-night Mediterranean cruise, this is €150–300 more per person — real money.

Daily gratuity: at approximately €15/person/day, Norwegian's service charge is higher than MSC/Costa's €10. For two people on 7 nights, that is €70 more.

Specialty dining costs: many of Norwegian's best dining experiences are specialty (paid), at €30–60/person. Budget for €200–400 in specialty dining for two people over a week to fully experience the food programme.

American character: Norwegian's style is unmistakably American — the language, the entertainment aesthetic, the food portions, the pace. European travellers who prefer a Mediterranean atmosphere may find this jarring.

Who Norwegian is for: independent travellers who dislike structure, foodies willing to pay for the extra quality, couples without children, anyone who has cruised before and found fixed dining restrictive, and travellers with a higher budget who want the best onboard experience in this price tier.

The other lines: where they fit

Royal Caribbean — entertainment first

If onboard activities and scale are the priority, Royal Caribbean is unmatched. Waterslides across 10 decks, surf simulators, zip lines, laser tag, mini-golf, ice skating, and Broadway shows — the ships are designed as destinations in themselves. The largest, Icon of the Seas, carries 7,600 passengers and displaces 250,000 tonnes.

Price: €549–800/person for 7 nights. Daily gratuity: ~€16/person.

Best for: families with teenagers, activity-obsessed travellers, and anyone who wants the "biggest ship in the world" experience.

Celebrity Cruises — premium without full luxury pricing

Celebrity positions itself one tier above Norwegian in terms of food, service, and design. The "Always Included" pricing bundles drinks, Wi-Fi, and gratuity into the base fare, simplifying budgeting. The main dining room food is considered the best in the standard-to-premium segment by most reviewers.

Price: €699–1,200/person for 7 nights (but with more included). Best for: couples, 40+ travellers, food enthusiasts, and anyone who finds the standard lines slightly disappointing.

Holland America operates mid-size ships with a mature, intellectually oriented culture. Longer itineraries, more port-intensive schedules, a strong culinary programme, and a conspicuously quieter onboard atmosphere. Less entertainment, more destination.

Price: €1,000–2,000/person. Best for: families with young children who are Disney fans. The premium is significant but the execution justifies it.

The decision framework

Answer these four questions and your choice becomes obvious:

1. Do you have children under 12? → MSC. The free children's places change the economics entirely.

2. Is the lowest possible price the priority? → Costa, then MSC. Norwegian is not the budget option.

3. Do you strongly dislike fixed dinner times? → Norwegian. Freestyle Dining is genuinely worth the premium for the right person.

4. Is food at dinner a priority? → Norwegian for variety, Costa for Italian quality, MSC for consistency.

If none of these apply and you are choosing your first cruise: start with MSC or Costa. Both are forgiving, well-priced, and operate itineraries from ports that are easy to reach. If you try one and want something different, Norwegian or Celebrity become the natural next step.

### Întrebări frecvente

Î: Which cruise line is cheapest — MSC, Costa or Norwegian?
R: Costa is typically the lowest base price, starting from €369–499/person for 7 nights in the Mediterranean. MSC is comparable at €399–599. Norwegian is 30–50% more expensive than both at €599–899/person. However, Norwegian sometimes includes more in the base fare (drinks, Wi-Fi, speciality dining) through its 'Free at Sea' promotions, which narrows the gap.

Î: Which cruise line has the best food?
R: Norwegian wins on variety and quality — 15–20 dining venues per ship, with speciality restaurants that genuinely rival upscale land restaurants. MSC and Costa both have good Italian food at the included dining room, with buffets of consistent quality. Celebrity Cruises (not in this comparison) is considered the industry leader for food quality in the premium segment.

Î: Which cruise line is best for families with children?
R: MSC leads for families. Children under 12 sail free on most MSC itineraries — a saving of €800–1,200 for a family of four. MSC also has age-specific kids' clubs (3–17), waterparks, and Cirque du Soleil shows. Royal Caribbean is comparable on facilities but more expensive. Disney Cruise Line is the premium family option at roughly double the price.

Î: What is Freestyle Dining and is it worth the extra cost on Norwegian?
R: Freestyle Dining means no fixed dinner time and no assigned table — you eat at any of Norwegian's venues whenever you want. Traditional cruise lines have two fixed dinner sittings (typically 6 PM and 8:30 PM). If you dislike the structure of fixed dining, Norwegian's flexibility is worth the 30–50% price premium. If you don't mind fixed times, MSC or Costa deliver comparable food at significantly lower prices.

Î: Do all three lines sail the Mediterranean?
R: Yes. All three have extensive Mediterranean programmes from May through October, with embarkation options from Italian ports (Civitavecchia/Rome, Genoa, Savona, Bari, Ravenna), Barcelona, and Athens. MSC and Norwegian have the most diverse itinerary options; Costa focuses primarily on the western and eastern Mediterranean with Italian ports as its main hubs.

Î: Can I book a cruise on these lines as a solo traveller?
R: Yes, but the single supplement is significant. Cabins are priced for double occupancy — solo travellers typically pay 100% of the double occupancy rate (i.e. full price for two, even occupying the room alone). Norwegian has some studio cabins designed for solo travellers on select ships, priced without the supplement. MSC and Costa occasionally run solo supplement discounts.

Î: Which line is easier to reach from Eastern Europe?
R: MSC from Civitavecchia (Rome) is the most accessible: direct flights from Bucharest, Warsaw, Prague, Budapest, and most Eastern European capitals take 1.5–2.5 hours. Costa from Savona (via Milan) is equally accessible. Norwegian's main Mediterranean embarkation points (Rome, Barcelona) are similarly reachable. All three are better options for Eastern European travellers than North American cruise lines based in Miami or Galveston.

Descriere: Detailed comparison of the best eSIM providers for European travel in 2026. Airalo, Saily, and Yesim compared on price, coverage, speed, and ease of use — with real prices and practical advice.

Răspuns scurt: For most European travellers in 2026, Airalo offers the best balance of price, coverage and reliability — plans start at $4.50 for 1GB/7 days. Saily (by NordVPN) is slightly cheaper in some regions and includes a built-in VPN. Yesim offers the widest coverage (200+ countries) and unlimited plans but at higher prices. All three work via eSIM — no physical SIM swap needed, setup takes 2-3 minutes, and you keep your regular number for calls while using data abroad.

Why you need an eSIM for European travel

If you're from outside the EU, your phone carrier probably charges €5-15 per day for roaming data in Europe. That's €35-105 for a week — just for the privilege of using Google Maps and WhatsApp. An eSIM solves this completely: you buy a data plan for €4-10, install it in 2 minutes, and you have fast local data for your entire trip.

Even if you're an EU resident with free roaming, an eSIM has advantages: guaranteed speed (no fair-use throttling), separate data for work/personal, and coverage in non-EU countries like Turkey, UK (post-Brexit), and the Balkans where roaming doesn't apply.

Airalo — best overall

Airalo is the largest eSIM marketplace in the world, and for good reason. The app is polished, installation takes under 3 minutes, and the plans are competitively priced. Their "Eurolink" regional plan covers 39 European countries including Turkey and the UK. Coverage uses Vodafone, Three, and other tier-1 carriers.

Best for: most travellers, first-time eSIM users, reliability.

Standout feature: you can top up your existing plan mid-trip without installing a new eSIM profile. This matters because some phones limit the number of eSIM profiles.

Weak point: no unlimited data plans. If you're a heavy data user (video calls, streaming), you'll burn through 5GB quickly.

Saily — best for privacy-conscious travellers

Saily is made by NordVPN (yes, the VPN company), which gives it a unique advantage: built-in VPN protection included with every plan. This means your data is encrypted automatically — useful on hotel WiFi, airport networks, and public hotspots.

Best for: privacy-conscious travellers, NordVPN subscribers, budget travellers (slightly cheaper per GB than Airalo on European plans).

Standout feature: the VPN is seamless — you don't need a separate app or subscription. It activates automatically when the eSIM connects.

Weak point: fewer countries covered (150+ vs 190+ for Airalo). Fine for Europe, but if you're also visiting Africa or Central Asia, check coverage first.

Yesim — best for heavy users and multi-continent trips

Yesim's differentiator is simple: they offer unlimited data plans. If you work remotely while travelling, join video calls, or stream content, Yesim's unlimited plan ($30/7 days or $55/30 days) removes all anxiety about data usage.

Best for: remote workers, digital nomads, heavy data users, round-the-world trips.

Standout feature: unlimited data with no throttling in most countries. Also covers 200+ countries — the widest coverage of the three.

Weak point: more expensive for light users. If you only need 1-3GB for maps and messaging, Airalo or Saily are better value.

How to install an eSIM — step by step

Before your trip (recommended):


Check your phone supports eSIM (iPhone XS or later, most Samsung/Pixel from 2020+)

Buy your plan through the provider's app or website

Scan the QR code or install the eSIM profile (Settings > Mobile Data > Add eSIM)

Label it "Travel" so you can tell it apart from your regular SIM

Keep it disabled until you land — it activates when you turn it on at your destination


At your destination:


Turn on the eSIM data plan in Settings

Set it as your primary data source

Keep your regular SIM active for calls/texts (or use WiFi calling)

That's it — you're connected


Total time: 2-3 minutes. No shop visit, no SIM swapping, no lost contacts.

Real-world tips

Buy before you fly. Some eSIM providers require an internet connection to install the profile. Do it on your home WiFi, not at the airport where WiFi may be spotty.

Screenshot your QR code. If anything goes wrong during installation, you'll need the QR code again. Save it to your photos.

Turn off carrier data roaming. This prevents your regular SIM from using expensive carrier data. Your eSIM handles all data; your regular SIM handles calls/texts only.

Check hotspot/tethering. If you're travelling with someone who doesn't have eSIM support, check that your plan allows hotspot sharing. Most do, but some budget plans restrict it.

Don't delete the eSIM profile. If you remove the profile, you may not be able to reinstall it. Just turn it off when you don't need it.

### Întrebări frecvente

Î: What is an eSIM and how does it work?
R: An eSIM is a digital SIM card built into your phone. Instead of swapping a physical SIM, you scan a QR code or install a profile, and you have a local data plan within 2-3 minutes. Your regular phone number stays active for calls and texts while the eSIM handles data. Most phones from 2020 onwards support eSIM (iPhone XS and later, Samsung Galaxy S20+, Google Pixel 4+).

Î: Is eSIM better than roaming in Europe?
R: If you're travelling within the EU with an EU SIM card, free roaming applies (with fair use limits). But if you're from the US/UK/outside EU, or your carrier charges for roaming, an eSIM is dramatically cheaper — €4-10 for a week vs €5-15 per DAY for carrier roaming. Even within the EU, an eSIM gives you a guaranteed fast data connection without worrying about fair use caps.

Î: Can I use WhatsApp and Google Maps with an eSIM?
R: Yes. An eSIM provides mobile data, so all data-based apps work normally: WhatsApp, Google Maps, Instagram, Uber, Bolt, Google Translate, and any other app. Calls and texts through your regular number still work via your primary SIM (you may pay roaming rates for those — use WhatsApp/FaceTime calls instead).

Î: Do I need to unlock my phone for eSIM?
R: No. eSIMs work independently of your physical SIM. However, your phone must support eSIM technology. Check by going to Settings > General > About and looking for 'EID' (iPhone), or Settings > Connections > SIM card manager (Android). If you see an eSIM option, you're set.

Î: Which eSIM provider has the best coverage in Europe?
R: All three major providers (Airalo, Saily, Yesim) cover the 30+ European countries most travellers visit. Airalo uses Vodafone and Three as primary carriers in most countries. Saily uses local tier-1 networks. Yesim has the widest raw coverage (200+ countries) which matters for multi-continent trips. For Europe-only travel, all three are equivalent in coverage.

## Best eSIM by Destination 2026: Turkey, USA, Thailand, UK and More

Descriere: Practical eSIM comparison for the most popular non-EU destinations. Real prices for Airalo, Saily and Yesim, what to avoid, and why you must buy before you leave.

Răspuns scurt: For destinations outside the EU, a prepaid eSIM with 5–10 GB costs between €8 and €20 for a week — far cheaper than roaming (€10–15/GB). Airalo, Saily and Yesim are the three most reliable providers. The single most important rule: buy before you leave. In Turkey, the authorities have blocked access to international eSIM provider websites since 2025, making it impossible to purchase once you are in the country.

Each destination has its own eSIM economics: how much data you actually use, which networks work well, and what local rules apply. Below is the practical comparison for the destinations European travellers visit most outside the EU, with prices verified in July 2026.

Three rules that apply everywhere

Before the destination-by-destination breakdown, three principles that do not change regardless of where you are going:

Buy before you leave. Install the eSIM at home on Wi-Fi. Activation happens automatically when you land and the phone connects to a partner network. Never plan on "I'll sort it when I get there" — some countries (Turkey specifically) make this impossible.

Enable data roaming on the eSIM profile. This sounds counterintuitive but is required. Without it, the eSIM plan does not connect to partner networks. It is a one-tap setting in your phone's SIM settings.

Keep your physical SIM for calls and bank codes. Use the eSIM only for data. Your Romanian number stays active for calls, and — crucially — for bank authentication SMS messages that many apps require.

Turkey

Turkey has a specific requirement that catches travellers off guard: since 2025, Turkish authorities block access to international eSIM provider websites (Airalo, Holafly, and others) for users already inside the country. If you try to purchase after arriving, the site simply does not load.

The solution is simple: buy and install before departure. The eSIM sits dormant on your phone until you land in Istanbul or Antalya, then connects automatically.

Which phones support eSIM

iPhone: eSIM available from iPhone XS / XS Max / XR (2018) onwards. iPhone 6, 7, 8, and X do not have eSIM.

Other Android: Inconsistent — some models in a range have eSIM, others do not, even in the same product line. Search "[your phone model] eSIM support" to confirm.

How to check on iPhone: Settings → General → About → if you see "EID" or "IMEI2" → eSIM supported.

How to check on Android: Settings → Network → SIM Manager → if "Add eSIM" option appears → supported.

Installing an eSIM — step by step

The process is the same regardless of provider:


Purchase the plan online (website or app) and pay by card

Receive a QR code by email

On iPhone: Settings → Mobile Data → Add eSIM → scan the QR code

On Android: Settings → Connections → SIM Manager → Add eSIM → scan QR code

The eSIM profile installs in 30–60 seconds

At your destination: go to SIM settings → select the eSIM profile → enable Data Roaming

Your phone connects to the partner network automatically


Install at home, on a good Wi-Fi connection. Do not attempt this at the airport or on 4G — the installation requires a stable connection and a moment of attention.

EU destinations — you do not need an eSIM

For completeness: if you are travelling within the EU, you almost certainly do not need an eSIM. EU roaming rules mean your Romanian plan works in all 27 EU member states plus Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein at no extra charge, subject to fair use limits (typically 15–30 GB/month of data roaming depending on your operator).

EU destinations where no eSIM is needed: Greece, Bulgaria, Croatia, France, Spain, Italy, Germany, Portugal, Austria, Czech Republic, Hungary, and all other EU countries.

The only exception: if your Romanian plan has a very small data allowance (under 5 GB/month) and you will be travelling for more than 2–3 weeks, buying additional EU roaming data or a local eSIM might be cheaper than your operator's overage charges.

For more on the eSIM vs roaming comparison in detail: eSIM vs roaming — when each makes sense .

For travel insurance that covers device loss (including your phone with that eSIM): travel insurance guide for Europe 2026 .

### Întrebări frecvente

Î: How much does an eSIM cost for a week in Turkey?
R: A 5 GB / 30-day plan for Turkey costs approximately $12 on Airalo. A 10 GB / 30-day plan costs around $18. For typical one-week usage (maps, WhatsApp, social media), 5 GB is enough. The critical requirement: buy before you arrive — Turkish authorities have blocked eSIM provider websites since 2025.

Î: Does Airalo work in Turkey?
R: Yes, but with one important condition: you must buy before you arrive. Since 2025, Turkish authorities have blocked access to major eSIM provider websites (including Airalo) for users already in the country. Install the eSIM at home, and it activates automatically when you land.

Î: Do I need an eSIM for Greece?
R: No. Greece is in the EU, and EU roaming rules apply — your Romanian mobile plan works in Greece at no extra charge (subject to fair use limits). You only need an eSIM for non-EU destinations like Turkey, UK, USA, Thailand, or Egypt.

Î: Do I need an eSIM for the UK after Brexit?
R: Yes. Since Brexit, the UK is no longer part of EU roaming, so your Romanian operator will charge non-EU rates — typically €3–7/day. A UK eSIM (5 GB / 15 days, ~$10–15 on Airalo) is much cheaper than roaming charges.

Î: How much data do I need in the USA for a week?
R: For typical use (maps, Uber, WhatsApp, social media, no streaming): 5–8 GB covers a week comfortably. If you use TikTok, Instagram Reels, or Netflix heavily, go for 10–15 GB. Note that US apps often autoplay videos — enable 'Data Saver' mode to reduce consumption.

Î: Are regional eSIM plans (e.g. 'Europe', 'Asia') cheaper?
R: Usually not per GB — regional plans are slightly more expensive per gigabyte than country-specific ones. But they are convenient if you are visiting 3+ countries on one trip (e.g. Thailand + Vietnam + Cambodia). For a single destination, the local plan is almost always cheaper.

Î: Can I use an eSIM and keep my regular SIM card?
R: Yes — that is exactly the point. Your phone has dual SIM capability: keep your Romanian physical SIM for calls and bank SMS codes, and use the eSIM for data. You activate the eSIM's data connection at the destination, and switch back to your Romanian SIM for calls.

## eSIM for Kids & Family Travel 2026: Do Children Need Their Own eSIM?

URL: https://plecari.com/en/esim-roaming/esim-for-kids-parents-guide
Limbă: English
Verticală: esim-roaming
Publicat: 2026-07-31
Actualizat: 2026-07-31
Versiunea RO: https://plecari.com/ro/esim-roaming/esim-pentru-copii-ghid-parinti

Descriere: eSIM for children 2026: which phones support it, best plans for families, hotspot sharing, parental controls and what to set up before the trip.

Răspuns scurt: Children don't automatically need their own eSIM. One parent's eSIM with a hotspot (mobile data sharing) active can cover the whole family's data needs — phones, tablets, and kids' devices all connect via Wi-Fi to the parent's hotspot. A child needs their own eSIM only if they need independent connectivity (separate phone, teen travelling with friends, or child staying with different family members). For a typical family holiday, 1 eSIM per adult with hotspot enabled (10–15 GB each) is the most practical and cost-effective solution.

Family holidays mean connectivity questions multiply: Does the 9-year-old need data on the iPad? Can the teenager be trusted with their own SIM? Does everyone need separate plans? And is there a cheaper way than buying data for 4 devices?

This guide answers all of it — practically, without jargon — so you can set up your whole family's connectivity before you leave the airport car park.

The Short Answer: One eSIM Per Adult, Hotspot for Everyone Else

Before getting into the detail, here's the practical answer that covers 90% of families travelling with children:

Buy one eSIM per adult. Enable hotspot on each adult's phone. Connect children's phones, tablets, and other devices to the hotspot.

That's it. No separate purchases for the kids, no fiddling with their devices, no age restrictions to navigate. Children connect to Mum's or Dad's hotspot the same way they connect to your home Wi-Fi. The data comes from your eSIM plan. You pay once per adult, not per device.

A 10 GB eSIM plan covers approximately: your navigation and messaging (2–3 GB), your children's tablets and casual use via hotspot (3–5 GB), plus a comfortable buffer. Total cost for a family of four: two eSIM plans at €8–16 each = €16–32 total for a week, versus four separate plans at €8–16 each = €32–64.

The exception — when a child genuinely needs their own eSIM — is covered further below.

What Is an eSIM and Why Does It Matter for Family Travel?

An eSIM (embedded SIM) is a digital SIM card built into the phone or tablet. Instead of buying a physical SIM card at the airport or paying expensive roaming fees to your home carrier, you:


Buy a data plan online before you travel (from Airalo, Saily, or Yesim)

Receive a QR code by email

Scan the QR code on the device — takes 2 minutes

Activate roaming data — the phone connects to local networks at the destination


No physical SIM to lose, no visit to a phone shop at the airport, no roaming bill surprise at the end of the trip. The family's home SIM cards stay in the phones for calls and messages — eSIM handles data only.

Why not just use carrier roaming?

If you're travelling within the EU from Romania, EU roaming is technically free — but with fair use limits that vary by carrier. Outside the EU (UK, Turkey, Egypt, USA, Thailand), your Romanian carrier charges €3–15 per device per day. For a family of four spending a week in London: €84–420 in roaming charges, versus €32–50 for two adult eSIMs covering everyone.

Setting Up the Family Hotspot — Step by Step

The hotspot is the key to covering the whole family with one eSIM purchase per adult. Here's exactly how to set it up:

On iPhone (any model with Personal Hotspot)


Go to Settings → Personal Hotspot

Toggle Allow Others to Join to ON

Note the Wi-Fi password shown on screen (or change it to something simpler)

On the child's device: go to Wi-Fi settings, find your phone's name, enter the password

Connected devices appear in your hotspot settings


Battery note: Running a hotspot uses more battery than normal browsing — expect 20–30% faster battery drain. Bring a portable charger (power bank) if you're doing full days out with the hotspot active.

Data note: All data used by connected devices counts against YOUR eSIM plan. A child streaming YouTube for 2 hours uses 1–2 GB of your data. Download videos on hotel Wi-Fi before heading out.

On Android (Samsung, Pixel, OnePlus, etc.)


Go to Settings → Connections (or Network & Internet )

Find Mobile Hotspot or Tethering

Toggle Mobile Hotspot ON

Tap the hotspot name to see or change the Wi-Fi password

On connected devices: join as a regular Wi-Fi network


Note: Some Android phones limit hotspot to 5–8 devices simultaneously. More than enough for a family.

Hotspot Range and Speed

Hotspot works within approximately 5–10 metres of the hosting phone. In practice: everyone at the same restaurant table, walking together on a tour, or in the same hotel room — all covered. If the family splits up during the day (one parent with younger children, another with a teenager), activate hotspot on both adults' phones.

Speed depends on your eSIM plan and local network. In most European cities and tourist destinations, expect 20–50 Mbps download — more than sufficient for navigation, video calls, and light streaming.

When Does a Child Actually Need Their Own eSIM?

The hotspot covers most situations. A child needs an independent eSIM in these specific circumstances:

1. Teenager travelling semi-independently
If your 16+ year-old is exploring a city on their own for part of the day (meeting friends, going to a concert, exploring a neighbourhood separately), they need their own data connection — not dependence on a parent's hotspot from 2 km away.

2. Child staying with different family members
Extended family trip where grandparents or relatives are in a separate accommodation or touring separately from the parents. Own eSIM = own connectivity.

3. Multiple-device families where hotspot battery is a concern
If you have 3+ children each with a device and both parents are heavy data users, the hotspot drain on two phones may be unsustainable for a full day of touring. Two eSIM plans plus two dedicated "children's" eSIM plans on the most data-heavy child devices may be more practical.

4. Child with a medical app requiring constant connectivity
Some medical devices (glucose monitors, specific apps for health management) require persistent data connectivity — not reliable through an intermittent hotspot.

eSIM for Tablets — iPad, Samsung Tab, and Others

Many families travel with a children's tablet (iPad, Samsung Galaxy Tab, Amazon Fire) for entertainment. Important distinction:

eSIM-compatible tablets (can have their own eSIM):


iPad Air (5th gen 2022+), iPad Pro (all models from 2018+), iPad mini (6th gen 2021+)

Samsung Galaxy Tab S7+, S8, S9 series (cellular versions)

Microsoft Surface Pro with LTE


Non-eSIM tablets (hotspot only):


Amazon Fire tablets (no eSIM support)

Most budget Android tablets

Wi-Fi-only versions of iPads and Samsung tablets


For an iPad with eSIM capability, you can install a children's eSIM directly on the iPad — no need to go through a parent's hotspot. But the hotspot approach is simpler and cheaper for most families.

Recommended approach for tablets: Connect to parent's hotspot. Download content (Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, games) on home or hotel Wi-Fi before going out. Children's tablets rarely need live data outside of maps and messaging.

Practical Tips for Family eSIM Setup

Install at home, not at the airport. Installation requires Wi-Fi. Do it the evening before departure at home, not in the departure lounge on airport Wi-Fi. If there's a problem (incompatible device, QR code issue), you have time to fix it.

Check eSIM compatibility before buying. Not all phones support eSIM. Check: iPhone Settings → General → About → look for IMEI2 or EID. Android: Settings → About Phone → SIM card status → check for eSIM. If a phone lacks eSIM, it can still connect via the parent's hotspot — it just can't have its own eSIM.

Set data limits on children's connected devices. On iPhone: Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy → App Limits. On Android: Settings → Digital Wellbeing. You can cap daily data usage so a child doesn't drain your hotspot allowance watching YouTube.

Download before you go. On the hotel/home Wi-Fi each evening, download:


Netflix/Disney+/YouTube episodes for the next day (offline mode)

Google Maps for your destination (offline maps)

Any large game updates


This dramatically reduces daytime data consumption via hotspot.

Keep your home SIM active for emergencies. Your Romanian SIM stays in your phone alongside the eSIM. If the eSIM fails or has no signal in a specific area, you can switch to your home SIM for an emergency call or message.

Bring a power bank. Running hotspot accelerates battery drain by 20–30%. A 10,000 mAh power bank is essential for a day of touring with children connected to your hotspot.

Beyond Data — Travel Insurance for the Family

eSIM sorts your data. Travel insurance sorts everything else. For families, travel insurance is especially important because:


Children are more likely to need medical attention (fever, ear infection, minor injuries)

Trip cancellation cover protects non-refundable family holiday costs (which are often much higher than adult-only trips)

Some family policies cover all children at no extra cost when both parents are insured


A family travel insurance policy from EKTA typically costs €30–60 for a week, covering 2 adults and dependent children together.

### Întrebări frecvente

Î: Does my child need their own eSIM on holiday?
R: Usually not. If your child uses a tablet or phone primarily for streaming, games, and messaging, connect them to a hotspot from your own eSIM. It's free (included in your data plan), works instantly, and you need zero extra purchases. Children need their own eSIM only if they have a separate phone and need independence from your device (e.g., teenagers exploring a city separately).

Î: What is an eSIM hotspot and how does it work?
R: A hotspot (also called mobile tethering or internet sharing) turns your phone's mobile data connection into a Wi-Fi signal that other devices connect to — exactly like a portable Wi-Fi router. On iPhone: Settings → Personal Hotspot → toggle on. On Android: Settings → Connections → Mobile Hotspot. Every device within 5–10 metres connects for free. Data used by connected devices counts against your eSIM data allowance.

Î: Can a child install an eSIM themselves?
R: Technically yes — eSIM installation is just scanning a QR code. But the purchase requires a payment card and the provider's app. For children under 16, the parent should purchase and install the eSIM. For older teens with their own phones, they can do it themselves if you buy the plan for them.

Î: Is there an age minimum for buying an eSIM?
R: eSIM purchases typically require an account with a valid payment method. Airalo, Saily, and Yesim require users to be 18+ to create an account and purchase plans. Parents buy and install on the child's behalf. There's no technical age restriction on using an eSIM in a phone — just on purchasing.

Î: How much data does a child need per day on holiday?
R: On holiday, children typically use: streaming (Netflix, YouTube offline — better to download at hotel): 1–3 GB/day. Social media scrolling (Instagram, TikTok): 200–500 MB/day. Gaming (most mobile games use little data, save for updates): 50–200 MB/day. Maps and messaging (WhatsApp, iMessage): 20–100 MB/day. For a typical holiday child usage (maps, messaging, light social, no streaming): 300–500 MB/day. 5 GB covers 10 days comfortably without streaming.

Î: Which phones support eSIM for children?
R: Most modern flagship phones from 2019 onwards support eSIM: iPhone SE (2020+), iPhone XS/XR and all subsequent models. Samsung Galaxy S20 and later, Galaxy A54, A73. Google Pixel 4 and later. Budget phones and older models may NOT have eSIM — check the device specifications before purchasing a plan. eSIM is separate from iPhones' iMessage — having eSIM doesn't give a child a phone number unless a calling plan is added.

Î: What's the best eSIM provider for family travel?
R: Airalo is the most practical for families: easy hotspot support on all plans, an excellent app, instant QR delivery, and plans for 190+ countries so one app covers every destination you visit. For Europe specifically, Saily's 'Europe' plan covering 30+ countries at competitive prices is excellent. Yesim's unlimited plans prevent bill shock if your teenager has high data habits.

Î: Does eSIM work in Turkey with children's devices connected via hotspot?
R: Yes, with one important caveat: buy the eSIM before entering Turkey. Since 2025, Turkish authorities block access to eSIM provider websites and apps from within Turkey. Buy and install the eSIM at home, before your flight. Once installed, it works fine in Turkey — and your hotspot works normally for all connected family devices.

## eSIM vs Roaming in 2026: complete guide with real prices

URL: https://plecari.com/en/esim-roaming/esim-vs-roaming
Limbă: English
Verticală: esim-roaming
Publicat: 2026-07-09
Actualizat: 2026-08-23
Versiunea RO: https://plecari.com/ro/esim-roaming/esim-vs-roaming

Descriere: Detailed eSIM vs roaming comparison with real 2026 prices per destination. Airalo, Saily, Yesim, Holafly compared — what to pick and how to avoid bill shock.

Răspuns scurt: Within the EU, roaming is free under 'roam like at home' rules — you use your home plan at no extra cost in all 27 EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. Outside the EU (Turkey, US, Thailand, Egypt, UK), carrier roaming can cost EUR 5-15 per MB. A prepaid eSIM costs USD 4-20 for 1-10 GB, saving you 80-95% compared to traditional roaming.

"eSIM or roaming?" is one of the first questions before any international trip. The short answer: within the EU, roaming is free and you don't need anything extra. Outside the EU, a prepaid eSIM costs 50-200 times less than your carrier's roaming rates.

Below you'll find the complete comparison with real prices from August 2026, for every popular destination, plus everything you need to know to choose, install, and use an eSIM without hassle.

Inside the EU: roaming is already free — no eSIM needed

Since 2017, the EU's "Roam Like at Home" (RLAH) regulation gives you the right to use your domestic mobile plan across all 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway at no additional cost. If you have 50 GB at home, you have 50 GB in Greece, Spain, or Italy too.

The regulation has been extended through June 30, 2032 , so there's no risk of it disappearing anytime soon.

Fair Use Policy — the data cap you should know about

There's a maximum amount of data you can use while roaming in the EU, but for most plans it's generous. The formula:

Fair-use cap (GB) = (domestic plan price in EUR / EUR 1.00) x 2

For a EUR 10/month plan, the roaming cap is 20 GB. For EUR 25/month, it's 50 GB. Since January 2025, the wholesale rate dropped to EUR 1.00/GB (from EUR 1.30), meaning higher fair-use caps for travelers.

Plan type Monthly cost Estimated roaming cap
Budget SIM-only EUR 5-8 ~12 GB
Mid-range plan EUR 15-20 ~34 GB
Premium / unlimited EUR 30-45 Effectively unlimited
Prepaid top-up EUR 10 (one-time) ~20 GB

If you exceed the cap, your carrier charges a maximum of EUR 2.00/GB — still reasonable. You'll receive notifications at 80% and 100% of your allowance.

Countries NOT covered by free EU roaming

This is where confusion costs real money:


Switzerland — surrounded by the EU but NOT in it and NOT in the EEA. Roaming here uses non-EU rates

United Kingdom — since Brexit (2020), the UK is no longer part of RLAH. Charged as a non-EU destination

Turkey — one of the most popular vacation destinations from Europe, but non-EU with expensive roaming

Albania, Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia — popular Balkan destinations, ALL non-EU

Egypt, Tunisia, Morocco — non-EU

United Arab Emirates (Dubai), USA, Thailand, Japan — non-EU


Simple rule: if the country isn't in the EU or EEA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway), roaming is NOT free.

Outside the EU: what carrier roaming actually costs

The numbers are shocking. European carriers charge non-EU roaming at rates that seem from another era:

Typical European carrier roaming rates (non-EU)

Zone Typical countries Data rate Cost per GB
Zone 2 (closer non-EU) Turkey, USA, Canada, UK EUR 5-15 per MB EUR 5,000-15,000
Zone 3 (rest of world) UAE, Asia, Africa EUR 8-20 per MB EUR 8,000-20,000

Read that again: a single GB in carrier roaming can cost EUR 5,000-15,000. If your phone downloads a 500 MB app update in the background, that's a EUR 2,500-7,500 bill. A 5 GB eSIM for the same destination costs USD 12-18.

Why this happens

European carriers don't have favorable wholesale agreements with networks outside the EU. The rates reflect real interconnection costs plus significant margins. It's a business model from the 2000s that hasn't adapted to the smartphone era — which is exactly why eSIMs have exploded in popularity.

What is an eSIM and how it works

An eSIM (embedded SIM) is a digital SIM card already built into your phone. It's not a physical object you insert — it's a software profile you download.

How it works, step by step


Buy a data plan online (website or app) before your trip

Receive a QR code via email or in the app

Scan the QR code in your phone's settings — the eSIM profile installs

Upon landing, your phone automatically connects to the local partner network

You have internet at local rates, up to 200 times cheaper than roaming


The key advantage: Dual SIM

The vast majority of modern phones support two SIMs simultaneously — physical SIM + eSIM. This means:


Your physical home SIM stays active for calls, texts, and bank verification codes (OTPs)

The eSIM handles internet exclusively, at local rates

Both work simultaneously — no need to remove one card to insert another


Setup takes 2-3 minutes in your phone's settings. Once installed, the eSIM activates automatically when you arrive at your destination.

Types of eSIM

Regional eSIM Group of countries (Europe, Asia, etc.) Multi-country tours USD 5-30
Global eSIM 100-170+ countries Frequent travelers, complex itineraries USD 15-50

When to choose each

How to install an eSIM — step-by-step guide

Before your trip (1-2 days before departure)

1. Check phone compatibility

Go to Settings > Network / SIM / Mobile Data . If you see an option to "Add eSIM" or "Add data plan," your phone is compatible.

eSIM-compatible phones (2026):

Brand Compatible models
Apple iPhone XS, XR, and all newer models (including SE 2, SE 3, 11-17, iPhone Air)
Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer, Z Flip/Fold all generations, A54, A55
Google Pixel 3 and all newer models (including Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 10)
Xiaomi 13, 14, 14T, 15, 15T, 17, 17T Pro
OnePlus 11, 12, 13, 13R, 15
Motorola Razr (2019+), Edge 50+, Edge 70
Sony Xperia 10 IV+, Xperia 1 V+, Xperia 5 V
Huawei P40 Pro, Mate 40 Pro
Nothing Phone 1, Phone 2, Phone 2a

Essential requirement: your phone must be carrier-unlocked . If you bought it on a carrier plan, check whether it's been unlocked. Phones purchased outright or from independent retailers are typically unlocked.

2. Buy the eSIM plan

Go to the website or app of your chosen provider (Airalo, Saily, Yesim):


Select your destination country or region

Choose a plan (GB + duration)

Pay with card (Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay)

Receive the QR code via email and in the app


3. Install the eSIM profile

On iPhone:


Settings > Mobile Data > Add eSIM > Scan QR Code

Or: Settings > Mobile Data > Add Data Plan > Scan QR Code

Label the profile: "Travel" or "Vacation" (so you can identify it easily)

Set mobile data to use the eSIM (not your physical SIM)


On Samsung / Android:


Settings > Connections > SIM Manager > Add eSIM

Scan the QR code

Label the profile

Set mobile data to eSIM


Important: do this at home, on Wi-Fi . Not at the airport, not on the plane, not at your destination. If something goes wrong, you have time to contact support.

At your destination


Enable data roaming on the eSIM profile (Settings > Mobile Data > eSIM > Data Roaming = ON). This sounds counterintuitive, but without this setting, the eSIM won't connect

Your phone detects the local network automatically — usually within seconds of landing

Verify that mobile data is set to eSIM, not your home SIM

Done — you have internet


When you return home


Disable the eSIM profile

Set mobile data back to your home SIM

You can delete the eSIM profile or keep it for your next trip to the same region


Destination-specific quirks — what you need to know

Turkey — BTK website blocks

Since July 2025 , Turkey's telecommunications authority (BTK) has blocked access to the websites and apps of major eSIM providers: Airalo, Holafly, Saily, Nomad, Instabridge, Alosim, BNESIM, Mobimatter, Ubigi, and Roamless . The block only applies to users inside Turkey — the websites work normally from any other country.

What this means in practice:


eSIMs purchased before arrival work perfectly — the block doesn't affect already-installed eSIMs

You CANNOT buy or top up an eSIM from within Turkey — the websites won't load

Buy 20-30% more GB than you think you need — you have no plan B if you run out

A VPN might bypass the block in some cases, but it's not guaranteed


Switzerland — the geographic trap

Switzerland is surrounded by the EU but is NOT part of free EU roaming. Many travelers flying to Geneva or Zurich assume roaming is included — and receive bills for hundreds of euros. A 3-5 GB eSIM for Switzerland costs USD 10-15 and eliminates the risk entirely.

Albania and the Western Balkans

Albania, Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia, Kosovo, and North Macedonia are extremely popular summer destinations. NONE are in the EU, so roaming is expensive. A regional "Europe" plan from Airalo or Saily usually covers these countries, but check each country individually — Albania and Kosovo can be missing from some packages.

USA — watch out for rural areas

US eSIM networks (T-Mobile, AT&T) are excellent in cities and along highways but can be weak in national parks, rural western areas, and some mountain zones. For a road trip, download offline maps and count on Wi-Fi in transit towns.

Dubai (UAE) — VoIP blocked

In the United Arab Emirates, VoIP services (WhatsApp Calling, FaceTime, Skype) are partially blocked or restricted. You can send WhatsApp text messages, but voice/video calls may not work without a VPN.

10 common eSIM mistakes

1. Buying the eSIM at the airport or after landing
In Turkey it's impossible (websites are blocked). In other countries, the stress of configuring at queues isn't worth it. Buy and install from home.

2. Confusing Switzerland or UK with the EU
Both are non-EU. Roaming is not free. An eSIM eliminates the risk.

3. Forgetting to enable "Data Roaming" on the eSIM
Without this setting, the eSIM won't connect. It's the most common cause of "my eSIM isn't working."

4. Leaving mobile data on your home SIM
After installing the eSIM, you must set mobile data to the eSIM profile, not your home carrier. Otherwise, you're consuming expensive carrier roaming.

5. Buying too little data
A 1 GB plan sounds cheap but runs out in 1-2 days if you use social media. Rule: minimum 3 GB per week for moderate users.

6. Not downloading offline maps
Google Maps uses 100-200 MB/hour during navigation. Offline maps = 0 MB. Save 1-2 GB over a one-week vacation.

7. Leaving photo sync on
Google Photos and iCloud can automatically upload photos to the cloud, consuming GBs without you realizing. Disable cloud upload on mobile data.

8. Comparing "unlimited" with "unlimited"
Many "unlimited" plans have a fair use policy: after 2-5 GB per day, speeds drop to 512 kbps (unusable for navigation or social media). A fixed 5-10 GB plan is more transparent.

9. Choosing a regional plan when a local one works
Regional plans (Europe, Asia) cost more per GB than single-country plans. If you're visiting one country, the local plan is always cheaper.

10. Ignoring free Wi-Fi
Hotels, cafes, restaurants, airports, metro systems — free Wi-Fi is everywhere in 2026. Use it for downloads, streaming, and video calls. The eSIM is for when you're on the move.

Special cases

Families with children

Options for connecting the whole family:


Hotspot from one phone: a single eSIM with a 10-20 GB plan, shared via hotspot with other phones/tablets. Cheapest option, but drains the source phone's battery

Individual eSIM on each phone: more expensive, but everyone has independent internet. Useful if you split up during the day

Tablets and older phones: if they don't support eSIM, connect them via hotspot from the phone with the eSIM


Tip: for kids on planes or at the hotel, download Netflix/YouTube/Disney+ content on Wi-Fi before departure.

Digital nomads and work-and-travel

If you work remotely, needs are different:


Minimum 15-20 GB per week (video calls, cloud, email with attachments)

Yesim unlimited (USD 8.40-57.60 for 1-30 days) or Holafly unlimited (USD 74.90 for 30 days) are the best options

A rented pocket Wi-Fi at your destination can be a more stable alternative for video conferences

Check whether the plan allows tethering/hotspot — not all do


Multi-country trips (3+ countries)

If you're visiting multiple countries on a single trip:


A regional plan (Europe 39 countries, Asia, etc.) is more convenient than separate country plans

Yesim global (5 GB / 30 days at USD 28.80, 147 countries) or Airalo global are solid options

The per-GB price is higher than local plans, but you gain simplicity


Cruises

On a cruise ship, onboard internet is expensive (USD 10-25/day) and slow. An eSIM works only in ports , when the ship is docked and your phone connects to the terrestrial network. At sea, the eSIM has no signal.

Optimal strategy: buy a regional plan covering the countries in your itinerary. Use onboard internet only for urgent messages. At each port, activate the eSIM and do everything you need (upload photos, messages, navigation).

WiFi Calling — the free alternative to roaming calls

WiFi Calling is a feature supported by most modern phones and carriers. When enabled, your phone uses Wi-Fi instead of the cellular network for calls and texts.

Why it matters for travelers

When you're outside the EU with an eSIM active for data only:


Incoming calls on your home SIM can generate roaming charges (your carrier charges for call forwarding)

WiFi Calling eliminates these charges — calls travel over the internet, not the cellular network

Works on hotel Wi-Fi and on the eSIM's data connection


How to enable

On iPhone: Settings > Phone > WiFi Calling > Enable on This iPhone
On Android: Settings > Connections > WiFi Calling > ON

Note: not all carriers support WiFi Calling while roaming. Check with your carrier before departure.

Alternative: WhatsApp/Telegram calls

If WiFi Calling isn't available, voice calls through WhatsApp or Telegram use only 35-50 MB/hour and are completely free. Audio quality is excellent on 4G/LTE. The only limitation: both parties need the app installed.

eSIM vs Pocket WiFi — which to choose

A Pocket WiFi (portable hotspot) is a small device you rent at your destination that provides Wi-Fi for up to 5-10 devices simultaneously.

Criterion eSIM Pocket WiFi
Cost USD 4-30 USD 5-15/day (rental)
Connected devices 1 (+ hotspot) 5-10
Battery Phone battery Separate battery (4-8 hours)
Setup 2-3 minutes, from home Pick up at airport or courier
Portability In your pocket Another object to carry
Works without charge Yes (it's on your phone) Needs to be charged and powered on

eSIM wins for: solo travelers, couples, anyone who wants maximum simplicity.
Pocket WiFi wins for: large groups (3+ people), families with many devices, anyone who needs stable internet for work.

Security and privacy — what to know

Are eSIMs secure?

Yes, equally secure as a physical SIM. The eSIM profile is stored in the phone's secure chip and cannot be cloned or copied without physical access to the device.

VPN — worth it with an eSIM?

Yes, in certain situations:


Public Wi-Fi (airport, cafe, hotel) — a VPN protects your data from interception

Dubai/UAE — VoIP (WhatsApp Calling, FaceTime) is blocked without a VPN

China — access to Google, WhatsApp, Instagram is blocked without a VPN


Saily includes basic VPN protection in its price. Yesim includes VPN on iOS. For full protection, a separate NordVPN or ExpressVPN subscription is recommended.

Is my personal data safe?

Reputable eSIM providers (Airalo, Saily, Yesim, Holafly) don't monitor or sell your browsing data. But — as on any network — unencrypted connections (HTTP, not HTTPS) can theoretically be intercepted. Use a VPN on public networks and check for HTTPS in your browser.

Additional FAQ

What's better: an eSIM or a local physical SIM?

eSIM wins on convenience: buy from home, no SIM swapping, keep your home number active. Local SIM wins on price: in some countries (Thailand, Vietnam, India), airport SIM cards are extremely cheap (USD 2-5 for 15-30 GB). But you need to remove your home SIM, lose incoming calls and texts, and sometimes need passport registration.

Does an eSIM work on a plane?

Not during flight (no cellular network at altitude). It activates automatically upon landing. Some planes have onboard Wi-Fi, but that's a separate service offered by the airline, unrelated to eSIM.

Can I have multiple eSIMs installed at once?

Yes. Most phones support 5-10 installed eSIM profiles, but you can only have 1-2 active simultaneously. You can have an eSIM for Turkey, one for the UK, and one for the US — activate them one at a time depending on your destination.

Does the eSIM drain extra battery?

Minimally. Two active SIM profiles (physical + eSIM) consume ~5-10% more battery per day than a single profile. The difference is negligible in practice.

What do I do if the eSIM doesn't connect at my destination?


Verify that "Data Roaming" is enabled on the eSIM profile

Check that mobile data is set to eSIM (not your home SIM)

Restart your phone

Manually select the network (Settings > Network > Manual operator selection)

Contact the provider's support via chat (on airport Wi-Fi)


Does the eSIM expire if I don't use it?

Validity typically starts at first network connection (upon landing), not at the time of purchase. Some plans also have an absolute expiration date (e.g., 90 days from purchase). Check the plan terms.

The bottom line — the 30-second rule


Traveling within the EU? You don't need anything — roaming is free

Traveling outside the EU? Buy an eSIM 1-2 days before departure

Going to Turkey? Buy the eSIM BEFORE you leave — provider websites are blocked in Turkey

How much to buy? 3 GB for a light week, 5 GB for moderate, 10 GB for heavy users

Which provider? Airalo for maximum flexibility, Saily for best value, Yesim/Holafly for unlimited


Search and compare eSIM plans for your destination below.

### Întrebări frecvente

Î: Do I need an eSIM within the EU?
R: Usually not. Since 2017, roaming in all 27 EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway is included in your home plan at no extra cost. An eSIM only makes sense if your plan has very limited data or you exceed the fair use cap (formula: plan price divided by EUR 1.00, multiplied by 2).

Î: How much does carrier roaming cost outside the EU?
R: Extremely expensive. European carriers typically charge EUR 5-15 per MB outside the EU — that translates to EUR 5,000-15,000 per GB. A single GB in carrier roaming costs more than 100-200 eSIM plans. An eSIM with 5 GB costs USD 12-18 for the same destinations.

Î: Can I keep my regular phone number while using an eSIM?
R: Yes. Modern phones support Dual SIM: your physical SIM stays active for calls, texts, and bank verification codes, while the eSIM handles mobile data. Both work simultaneously. Setup takes 2-3 minutes in phone settings.

Î: Does my phone support eSIM?
R: Most phones from 2018 onward: iPhone XS/XR and newer, Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer, Google Pixel 3 and newer, Xiaomi 13+, OnePlus 11+. Check Settings > Network/SIM for an 'Add eSIM' option. Your phone also needs to be carrier-unlocked.

Î: How much data do I need for a one-week vacation?
R: Depends on usage. Light (maps + WhatsApp): 1-2 GB. Moderate (+ social media, Uber): 3-5 GB. Heavy (+ Instagram Reels, TikTok): 5-7 GB. Digital nomad (remote work): 10-20 GB. Add a 20-30% buffer for background apps.

Î: What if I run out of data on my eSIM while traveling?
R: Buy an additional plan from the provider's app (Airalo, Saily, Yesim) — installs in 2 minutes on hotel Wi-Fi. EXCEPTION: in Turkey, you cannot purchase eSIMs from inside the country (websites are blocked by the BTK regulator). This is why buying enough data before departure is critical.

## How to Install an eSIM on iPhone or Android: Step-by-Step Guide 2026

URL: https://plecari.com/en/esim-roaming/how-to-install-esim
Limbă: English
Verticală: esim-roaming
Publicat: 2026-07-29
Actualizat: 2026-07-29
Versiunea RO: https://plecari.com/ro/esim-roaming/cum-instalezi-esim

Descriere: Exact steps to install an eSIM on iPhone and Android, which phones support it, common errors and fixes, and how to set up dual SIM so you keep your regular number while using local data.

Răspuns scurt: Installing an eSIM takes 2–3 minutes: buy a plan from a provider like Airalo or Saily, receive a QR code by email, go to your phone's SIM or mobile data settings, select 'Add eSIM', scan the QR code, and the profile downloads automatically. Do this at home on a stable Wi-Fi connection before your trip. The eSIM sits dormant until you land and activate it — your regular SIM stays active for calls and SMS the entire time.

An eSIM is the most practical way to get mobile data abroad without paying roaming charges or hunting for a SIM card kiosk at the airport. The technology sounds complicated — digital SIM, QR codes, profiles — but the actual process takes under five minutes. Here is exactly how it works on every device type, plus every error you might encounter and how to fix it.

Before you start: three things to check

1. Does your phone support eSIM?

Not every phone has eSIM capability. Check before purchasing a plan:

Brand eSIM-compatible models
iPhone XS, XS Max, XR (2018) and all newer models
iPhone — no eSIM 6, 7, 8, X, SE 1st gen
Samsung Galaxy S20 series and newer; Z Fold/Flip series; some A-series from 2022
Google Pixel 3 and newer
Other Android Varies by model — check settings (see below)

Quick check — any phone: dial *#06# . If you see an EID number in the list that appears, your phone supports eSIM.

iPhone check: Settings → General → About → scroll down. If you see EID or IMEI (eSIM) , eSIM is available.

Android check: Settings → Connections (Samsung) or Network & Internet (Pixel/stock Android) → SIM card manager or SIM cards → if you see an Add eSIM option, the phone supports it.

Important caveat: phones sold in mainland China, Hong Kong, and some other markets may have eSIM hardware but with eSIM functionality disabled at the firmware level by the manufacturer for that market. Even if the model generally supports eSIM elsewhere, the China-market version may not. If you are unsure, check with the manufacturer for your specific model and market variant.

2. Is your phone carrier-unlocked?

eSIM support and carrier-unlocked status are separate requirements. A phone tied to a specific carrier (typically bought on contract) may be locked to that carrier's SIMs — including eSIM. You need both eSIM support AND an unlocked phone.

How to check if unlocked: try inserting a SIM from a different operator. If it works — unlocked. If you get "SIM not supported" or "Enter unlock code" — locked.

How to unlock: contact your current carrier. Most unlock phones after the contract period (typically 12–24 months). The process is usually free and takes 1–5 business days. Do this before your trip — not the night before departure.

3. Do you have the QR code ready?

You receive the QR code by email after purchasing your eSIM plan. Have it open on a second device (laptop, tablet) or printed — you will scan it with the camera of the phone you are installing it on.


How to install an eSIM on iPhone — step by step

Method 1: Scan QR code (most common)


Open Settings

Tap Mobile Data (or Cellular on US devices)

Tap Add eSIM (or Add Mobile Plan )

Tap Use QR Code

The camera opens — point it at the QR code from your provider's email

When the plan is detected, tap Continue

Tap Add Mobile Plan on the confirmation screen

Choose a label for the plan (e.g. "Travel" or the destination name) — this helps distinguish it from your main SIM

Choose what this plan is used for: select Mobile Data (leave calls and SMS on your regular SIM)


The profile downloads — typically 10–30 seconds on a good Wi-Fi connection. When the download completes, the plan appears in your SIM list as inactive.

Method 2: Install from image on phone (iOS 17.4+)

If the QR code image is already on your iPhone (saved to Photos, or visible in an email on the same phone):


Long-press the QR code image

Tap Add eSIM in the menu that appears

Continue from step 6 above


This method avoids needing a second device to display the QR code.

Method 3: Manual entry (if QR code is not working)


In the Add eSIM screen, scroll to the bottom

Tap Enter Details Manually

Copy and paste the SM-DP+ Address and Activation Code from the provider's email

Tap Next and proceed with the installation


This is useful when the QR code has already been scanned once (making it invalid) or when image quality is poor.


How to install an eSIM on Android — step by step

The menu path varies slightly between manufacturers but the process is identical.

Samsung Galaxy (One UI):


Settings → Connections → SIM card manager

Tap Add eSIM

Tap Scan QR code from service provider

Scan the QR code from the email

Tap Confirm when the plan details appear

The profile downloads — tap Done

In SIM card manager: tap the new eSIM → set as Mobile Data SIM

Enable Data Roaming on the eSIM profile


Google Pixel (stock Android):


Settings → Network & Internet → SIMs

Tap + (Add SIM) or Add eSIM

Tap Download a SIM instead? if prompted, or select the scan option

Scan the QR code

Confirm and download

Set the eSIM as your data SIM in the settings that follow


Other Android (Xiaomi, OPPO, Motorola, OnePlus):

Look under: Settings → Network & Internet or Mobile Network or Connections . Search for "SIM" in your settings search bar if you cannot find it. The option may be labelled "Download eSIM," "Add eSIM," or "SIM card manager."


After installation: the critical settings

Installing the eSIM profile is step one. These two settings determine whether it actually works:

Step 1 — Set the eSIM as your data SIM

On iPhone: Settings → Mobile Data → Mobile Data (scroll down to the list) → select your travel eSIM as the data line.

On Android: Settings → Connections → SIM card manager → select the eSIM → set as Mobile Data .

Without this, your phone continues using your regular SIM for data (and incurring roaming charges from your home carrier).

Step 2 — Enable Data Roaming on the eSIM profile

This is the most commonly missed step and the most frequent reason eSIMs "don't work" after installation.

On iPhone: Settings → Mobile Data → tap the eSIM plan name → enable Data Roaming .

On Android: Settings → Connections → SIM card manager → tap the eSIM → enable Data Roaming or International roaming .

This setting tells the phone it is allowed to connect to partner networks abroad (which is the entire point of the eSIM plan). Without it, the phone is installed but refuses to connect.


The dual SIM setup: keep your regular number AND use the eSIM

This is the optimal configuration for travel. Most people set it up once and never need to change it:

Function Which SIM
Mobile data Travel eSIM
Calls (outgoing) Physical SIM (your regular number)
SMS Physical SIM
Bank verification codes Physical SIM (they go to your regular number)
WhatsApp / messaging apps Either (uses data from the eSIM)

The result: you pay local data rates through the eSIM while still being reachable on your normal number and receiving SMS codes from your bank without extra charges.

iPhone dual SIM setting: Settings → Mobile Data → tap each function (Data, Calls, Messages) and assign which SIM to use.

Android dual SIM setting: Settings → Connections → SIM card manager → set default SIM for Data, Calls, and Messages separately.


Common errors and how to fix them

"Unable to activate eSIM" or "Download failed"

Most common cause: unstable Wi-Fi. The download requires a consistent connection — the airport Wi-Fi or a crowded café network frequently causes this.

Fix: move to a more reliable Wi-Fi network, restart the phone, and try again. If you are at home, restart your router as well.

"QR code cannot be read"

Causes: poor image quality, screen brightness too low on the device displaying the QR, or the code has already been activated.

Fixes: increase brightness on the device showing the QR code, move to a brighter environment, ensure the camera has good focus. If the code was already scanned (even partially), contact the provider — they will issue a replacement code.

"SIM not supported" or no eSIM option in settings

Causes: the phone does not support eSIM, the eSIM functionality is disabled (China/HK market variants), or the phone is carrier-locked.

Check eSIM support via *#06# (EID number present = supported). If supported but the option is missing, contact your carrier — the phone may need to be unlocked.

eSIM installed but no data connection

Almost always caused by one of two things:


Data Roaming not enabled on the eSIM profile (see "critical settings" above)

eSIM not set as the data SIM (the phone is using the regular SIM for data)


Check both settings. If both are correct: disable and re-enable the eSIM profile, restart the phone. If still no connection, contact the eSIM provider's support — there may be a network provisioning issue.

"This SIM is not from this carrier" error on installation

Your phone is carrier-locked. The eSIM cannot be installed until the phone is unlocked. Contact your home carrier.

eSIM plan shows "No service" in the destination country

The eSIM plan may not include the specific country you are in, or the partner network in that country is experiencing an outage. Check the plan details on the provider's app — the list of supported networks is usually listed. If the country is included: manually select the network (Settings → Mobile Data → Network Selection → Manual → find a listed partner network).


When to install: before or after departure?

Always install before departure. Here is why:

If you install at home:


You have a stable Wi-Fi connection

If anything goes wrong, you have time to troubleshoot or contact support

The eSIM profile sits dormant on the phone — it does not generate any charges until you activate it

At the destination, you simply enable it — 5 seconds


If you wait until you arrive:


Airport Wi-Fi is often unreliable and crowded — downloads fail

You are tired after a flight and less patient with troubleshooting

If the QR code fails, you have no data to contact support

Some destinations (Turkey, notably) block access to eSIM provider websites — you cannot even buy a plan from within the country


One exception: if your provider allows installation via their app with a cellular-data-independent method, you might be able to install later. But the default recommendation remains: install at home, 1–2 days before departure.


Which eSIM to buy

For most destinations, three providers cover the majority of needs:

Airalo — the largest aggregator. Sources plans from hundreds of local providers, offering the most options per country. Best for destinations where you want maximum flexibility or are visiting somewhere unusual. Browse plans on Airalo .

Saily — NordVPN's eSIM product. Includes a basic VPN for public Wi-Fi security (useful in cafés and airports). Competitive pricing for major destinations. Browse plans on Saily .

Yesim — strong regional plans for Europe and Asia. Worth comparing for multi-country trips where a single regional plan beats buying per-country. Browse plans on Yesim .

How to choose: compare prices for your specific destination on all three before buying. The cheapest for Turkey in a given month may be different from the cheapest for the US. Differences are usually €2–5 for a standard week's plan — not enormous, but worth the 2-minute comparison.

For a full comparison by destination (Turkey, UK, USA, Thailand, Egypt, Japan): best eSIM by destination 2026 .

For the comparison of eSIM vs roaming — when each option makes more sense: eSIM vs roaming .


After the trip: managing installed eSIM profiles

After you return, the eSIM profile remains on your phone. Options:

Leave it installed (recommended): the profile is inactive and generates no charges. If you return to the same destination, you do not need to reinstall — just reactivate and, if the plan has expired, top up or buy a new plan from the same provider.

Delete the profile: Settings → Mobile Data → tap the eSIM → Delete eSIM. Note: once deleted, the profile cannot be recovered. You would need to purchase a new plan and reinstall for future trips.

Turn it off without deleting: Settings → Mobile Data → tap the eSIM → toggle off Turn On This Line . The profile remains installed and inactive — zero impact on your phone's operation.

Most frequent travellers accumulate several eSIM profiles for their regular destinations — one for Turkey, one for the US, one for the UK — and simply activate the relevant one before each trip.

### Întrebări frecvente

Î: Does my phone support eSIM?
R: iPhone: XS, XR and all newer models (from 2018). iPhone 6, 7, 8, and X do not have eSIM. Samsung: Galaxy S20 and newer, Z Fold/Flip series. Google Pixel: 3 and newer. Quick check: dial *#06# — if an 'EID' code appears in the list, your phone supports eSIM. On iPhone: Settings → General → About → look for 'EID'. On Android: Settings → Connections or Network → if 'Add eSIM' appears, you have support.

Î: Do I need Wi-Fi to install an eSIM?
R: Yes. The phone downloads the eSIM profile from the provider's servers, which requires an internet connection. Install at home on your own Wi-Fi before the trip. If you are already abroad without data, you can install via a hotel or café Wi-Fi, but it is much simpler to do it in advance.

Î: Can the QR code be scanned more than once?
R: No. Most eSIM QR codes are single-use — once scanned and the profile installed, the code is deactivated. If you scan it and the installation fails (poor Wi-Fi, phone restart mid-process), contact the provider. Most will issue a new code for free for genuine installation failures.

Î: How do I activate the eSIM when I land?
R: The eSIM profile is installed but inactive until you turn it on. When you land: go to Settings → Mobile Data (iPhone) or Connections → SIM Manager (Android) → select your eSIM profile → enable it as the data SIM. Also ensure 'Data Roaming' is enabled on the eSIM profile — without this, the eSIM connects to partner networks but no data flows.

Î: Can I keep my regular number while using an eSIM?
R: Yes — that is the primary advantage of eSIM. Your physical SIM stays active for calls, SMS, and bank verification codes. The eSIM handles data. Both work simultaneously with dual SIM. Set data to the eSIM, calls and SMS to your physical SIM, and you have the best of both: local data rates and your regular number.

Î: What if my phone is carrier-locked?
R: A carrier-locked phone cannot use SIM cards from other operators, including eSIM profiles. eSIM support and being carrier-unlocked are separate requirements — you need both. Contact your carrier to unlock the phone (usually free after the contract period ends). Note: this does not apply to carrier-locked eSIM functionality — if your carrier has locked eSIM access, it needs to be unlocked separately.

Î: Can I use an eSIM in Turkey?
R: Yes, but you must buy and install it BEFORE arriving in Turkey. Since 2025, Turkish authorities block access to major eSIM provider websites (Airalo, Saily) from within Turkey. The eSIM profile installed at home works normally once you land in Istanbul or Antalya.

Î: How long does an eSIM plan last?
R: Plans are typically sold with a fixed data allowance and a validity period: for example, 5 GB valid for 30 days from activation. The plan expires when you use all the data OR when the validity period ends — whichever comes first. Some providers offer 'top up' options if you run out of data before the period ends.

The eSIM market has matured rapidly. Three years ago, travellers who wanted local data abroad had two realistic options: buy a local SIM at the airport (involving a SIM swap and potentially losing access to their regular number) or pay expensive carrier roaming rates. Today, a prepaid eSIM installed at home in three minutes is the standard approach — and the question is which provider to use.

Saily, developed by Nord Security (the company behind NordVPN), entered this market in 2023. By 2026, it has established itself as a credible third option alongside Airalo (the market leader) and Yesim. This review covers what Saily actually offers, where it performs well, where it falls short, and how to decide between the three — with real 2026 prices.


What Saily is

Saily is a prepaid eSIM service that provides mobile data in 150+ countries . The mechanics are identical to any eSIM provider:


Purchase a plan on saily.com or in the Saily app

Receive a QR code by email (instantly)

Scan the QR code in your phone's SIM settings

The eSIM profile installs in 30–60 seconds

At your destination: activate the eSIM profile and enable Data Roaming


Your primary SIM (physical) remains active throughout — you retain your regular phone number for calls and SMS while the eSIM handles data.

What makes Saily different from other providers

Built-in VPN. The main differentiator versus Airalo and Yesim is the VPN layer inherited from NordVPN's technology. Saily automatically encrypts your connection on unsecured public Wi-Fi networks (hotels, cafés, airports). It also includes:


Ad blocker — blocks web advertisements, reducing data consumption by up to 28.6% according to Saily's own measurements

Web protection — automatically blocks access to known malicious domains (phishing, malware distribution)

115+ virtual locations — you can appear to be browsing from another country


For travellers who regularly use hotel Wi-Fi, airport networks, or café hotspots, this is a meaningful differentiator — it adds a layer of security without requiring a separate VPN app or subscription.

Most generous unlimited data threshold. On unlimited plans, Saily offers 5 GB/day at full speed before throttling to ~1 Mbps. This is the highest threshold on the market: Airalo offers 3 GB/day, and Nomad only 2 GB/day. For most travellers, 5 GB/day covers maps, social media, messaging, and even moderate video streaming.
